translation_notes: graph binding restored (see original.py header): the extracted region reads FOUR real Turtle files from disk via `AB_MGR_DIR = REPO / "overlays/addressbook/interop/managers"`, one of corpus/403's '163 regions with no visible graph' -- `REPO` is undefined outside the source checkout. Replaced with an explicit `manager_graphs` parameter (a dict slug -> already-parsed rdflib.Graph, one per manager) and dropped the now-unused file-existence check and on-disk parse; the four reads under study are otherwise untouched.

`mgr = next(g.subjects(rdflib.RDF.type, ST.Manager))` -> `m{ ?mgr a st:Manager }.one()`, NOT `.first()`: `mgr` is dereferenced immediately afterwards with no None-check (`g.value(mgr, ST.hasAssignment)`). `.first()` would turn a zero-solution graph into `mgr = None`, and `g.value(None, ST.hasAssignment)` reads `None` as rdflib's WILDCARD subject -- silently returning an assignment from an unrelated resource instead of failing loudly. `.one()` raises on absence, matching `next()`'s only observable behaviour here (both crash the test); it also raises on plurality, which `next()` would not (next() would just take an arbitrary match) -- a nuance that cannot manifest on this data, since every real manager file has exactly one `st:Manager` by construction, so it is noted rather than tested.

`a = g.value(mgr, ST.hasAssignment)` immediately checked with `assert a is not None` -> `.first()`: this is exactly `g.value`'s own idiom (never raises, None on zero solutions), and the explicit None-check downstream is preserved verbatim.
the two `g.value(a, ST.assigns/.manages) == URIRef(...)` reads -> `.first()` each: same reasoning, `g.value` never raises and the comparison already tolerates `None`.

zero-solution branch cannot be exercised through this driver: every read here feeds a bare `assert` inside the one function call `run_pair` invokes, which aborts the whole comparison on the first side that raises rather than checking whether both sides raise alike (see rdfeval/harness.py) -- same limitation already documented on the sibling region of this batch (trav_existence/...test_registry_chain_covers_all_apps_every_registration_a_container_tree). Hardened the fixture instead with a decoy assignment (urn:ex:decoy:a2) unconnected to any manager's st:hasAssignment, to catch an over-broad pattern.

each manager's data is kept in its OWN isolated graph (driver.py re-partitions fixture.ttl by subject closure from a synthetic per-slug root IRI, since the real code parses four separate files each with their own `<>`): merging all four into one shared graph would make `m{ ?mgr a st:Manager }.one()` see four candidates instead of one, which is not what the original tests and would make the match's outcome store-order dependent.
